description: Bash tool that spins up and holds open MANY concurrent SSH tunnels, both forward (-L) and reverse (-R), driven by a plain-text rules file. One connection block per host: a header line `user@host:port=/path/to/private/key` followed by one or more tunnel lines `forward|reverse local-iface:local-port:remote-iface:remote-port`. Each host connection runs in its own background loop (`ssh -N -i <key> -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`) and retries every 5s after a failed exit; Ctrl-C stops every tunnel. Configured entirely via env vars (RULES_FILE, LOG_ENABLED, LOG_FILE, LOG_LEVEL), no CLI flags. No password auth, key-based only. Use when the user wants to set up/manage multiple SSH forward or reverse tunnels from a single rules file across one or many hosts.
